claim.summary: Over F2, for every m>n>=0, the Boolean rank equations AB=I_m admit an explicit Hilbert-like IPS certificate built with one shared child of shape (m-1,n-1), first-nonzero pivot selectors and all Boolean mux/field corrections. Size obeys S(m,n)<=S(m-1,n-1)+poly(m,n), and depth O(n); joint placeholder degree is at most 3^n(n+1)!. Normalization gives a full residual certificate of polynomial size and depth O(n), with no constant-depth guarantee or original-PC-degree preservation. A seven-fixture native Singular checker verifies all local matrix/field maps and negative controls.
claim.assessment: Working explicit shared recurrence and complete Boolean certificate ledger passed by the sole medium reviewer. Direct Hilbert-like normalization additionally lies in the (m-1)-st power of the matrix-B ideal, so fixed-order B jets at B=0 vanish for large m; this is not a statement about arbitrary residual representatives. No new general rank-principle IPS upper-bound novelty claimed.

claim.summary: For the exact shared-pivot Hilbert-like certificate C_(m,n), its Y_(n+1,n+1) coefficient is the Gaussian pivot-success function of the first n rows of A, hence the binary determinant function on that square submatrix. At m=2n this particular certificate polynomial has no polynomial-size uniformly fixed-depth binary arithmetic circuit, by the recorded determinant-function lower bound. This does not lower-bound other certificate representatives or the normalized Boolean residual Q obtained from C.
